title: Certificates of Deposit: Interest Accrual, Crediting Dates and Where Interest Goes
content:
This page explains how interest on Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit builds up day by day, on which dates it is credited, and what the owner may choose to have done with it.

## Daily accrual

Interest accrues for every calendar day of the term, beginning with the term start date and ending with the day before the maturity date. Each day's interest is the principal balance at the end of that day, multiplied by the certificate's interest rate, divided by 100 and divided by the tier's number of days in the year. Compounding is daily: the interest accrued on one day becomes part of the base on which the next day's interest is figured.

## Crediting dates

- **Monthly crediting:** accrued interest is credited on the last calendar day of every month, and the final partial month is credited on the maturity date.
- **Crediting at maturity:** one credit covering the whole term is made on the maturity date.
- Daily accruals are kept unrounded; only the total for the period is rounded, half-up to the cent, when it is credited.
- When the owner takes a full early withdrawal, interest accrued but not yet credited is credited on that day, and that credit forms part of the balance on which the penalty for that withdrawal is figured.

## Where credited interest goes

- **Compounding:** the credit is added to the certificate's principal.
- **Paid to checking or to savings:** the credit is sent to the payout account named on the certificate and the certificate's principal stays as it was. The payout account must be the owner's own account and must be active; when it is not, that period's interest compounds into the certificate instead.
- The owner may select only a choice the tier lists.

## Tier settings

| Tier | Compounding | Days in the year | Crediting | Choices for credited interest | Grace days earn interest on money withdrawn in grace |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | daily | 365 | at maturity | compound only | No |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | daily | 365 | monthly | compound, pay to checking, pay to savings | No |
| 12-Month Certificate | daily | 365 | monthly | compound, pay to checking, pay to savings | No |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | daily | 365 | monthly | compound, pay to checking, pay to savings | No |
| 36-Month Certificate | daily | 365 | monthly | compound, pay to checking, pay to savings | No |
| 60-Month Certificate | daily | 365 | monthly | compound, pay to checking, pay to savings | No |

## Interest across the grace period

Because no tier lets grace days earn interest on money taken out during grace, money withdrawn during the grace period earns nothing for the grace days before it leaves. Balance carried into a renewed term earns that term's rate for every day from the maturity date on.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A certificate holds USD 10000.00 at an assumed rate of 4.00 percent on a 365-day year, with no deposits or withdrawals.

- Day 1: 10000.00 multiplied by 4.00, divided by 100, divided by 365, gives 1.0958904 of interest.
- Day 2: the base is now 10001.0958904, giving 1.0960105.
- If the period ended after these two days, the unrounded total of 2.1919009 would be credited as USD 2.19.
